speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A physics reading programme
summary: The opening question is \ru{Что надо знать из физики?}; an uncertain marginal attribution says ``following Sinai?''. The programme lists classical and Hamiltonian mechanics; quantum mechanics and scattering; relativity and field theory; and quantum field theory, including second quantization, Bose and Fermi statistics, functional integrals, perturbation series, Feynman diagrams, renormalization and Yang--Mills fields. Arnold, Landau--Lifshitz, Fermi, Weinberg and Hepp are reading suggestions. Consultation with physicists and a typed version are requested. No theorem, calculation or definite research problem is stated, so the programme is preserved without manufacturing mathematical occurrences. Gindikin begins on the same page; the catalogue's P000659--P000660 window overlaps that next record.

speaker: S. G. Gindikin, with I. M. Gelfand
title: SL(2, R), integral geometry and analytic separation of series
summary: The group is represented as the determinant-one quadric, and the regular representation is studied through hyperplane and line integrals. Gelfand distinguishes separation into series from decomposition into individual irreducibles. The announced real-transform kernels isolate discrete and continuous parts; two complex domains then realize the positive and negative discrete parts as Hardy boundary values. The lecture ends with an explicit kernel and Arnold's conjecture identifying the domains by their fractional-linear action. The exact subsequent paper is \citet{gelfandgindikin1977complex}, received 6 June 1977. Its kernel has an additional nonconstant factor absent from the notebook. P000661--P000662 unmistakably continue this lecture, despite the catalogue's narrower page window.

speaker: Academic-year heading
summary: This catalogue entry labels the academic year and overlaps the opening lectures. It supplies no separately identifiable mathematical exposition. The actual occurrences in its page window belong to records 397--398 and 400--403 and are indexed there once.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Superalgebras, supergroups and supermanifolds: announced heading
summary: Immediately below the date 13/IX-76, the manuscript gives Kirillov's name and this title, then explicitly switches to Fuchs and the Weil algebra. No intervening exposition is recorded. The title is retained as a programme heading; Fuchs's formulas and Kirillov's later intervention are assigned to records 401 and 402. The broad catalogue window P000662--P000664 must not be read as an independent three-page Kirillov lecture.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: The Weil algebra and its differential
summary: Fuchs constructs the graded algebra \(\Lambda\mathfrak g^*\otimes S\mathfrak g^*\), specifies its differential on generators, explains the signed Leibniz rule and gives the structure-constant formula on the symmetric generators. The concluding acyclicity statement omits the surviving degree-zero constants. Characteristic classes are announced for a future meeting, not developed here. This is established Weil--Cartan theory: \citet{cartan1950weil,cartan1950transgression}. The lecture begins on P000663 and ends before the explicit Kirillov intervention on P000664.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Transgression and invariant forms on compact Lie groups
summary: A short intervention explains the purpose of the Weil algebra in computing compact Lie-group cohomology. The intended correspondence is between primitive odd cohomology generators and indecomposable symmetric invariant polynomials. The notebook states a stronger, false dimension equality for all invariant forms and reverses the differential direction in its transgression shorthand. The surrounding Fuchs and Arnold lectures belong to separate records.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Point equivalence of second-order equations and projective geometry
summary: Arnold explicitly revisits nineteenth-century work of Lie, Tresse and Liouville and Cartan's 1924 projective connections. The lecture separates point linearization, pairs of line fields in a contact three-manifold, projective parameters along solutions, and inequivalent projective structures on a circle. It then normalizes the quadratic transverse terms, obtains a relative 5/2-density, and constructs projective scalar invariants from its reciprocal power. A damaged global question and Gelfand's proposed cohomological connection are recorded without inventing missing quantifiers. The local normalization calculations can be checked, but the stated flatness implication needs additional hypotheses.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Lie superalgebras and the Wess--Zumino multiplet
summary: Novikov explicitly recommends Ogievetsky's UFN review and a Zumino review, with Volkov and Akulov noted in the margin. He defines Lie superalgebras, uses real Majorana spinors to construct supertranslations, and records Gelfand's request to adjoin Lorentz generators. The Wess--Zumino chiral multiplet, its auxiliary fields, Lagrangian and infinitesimal transformations occupy the remainder. The material predates the talk, as the cited 1975 review confirms. Several faithful notebook errors require emendation: Gol'fand's name, the scalar label on the spinor, an uncontracted kinetic index, and incompatible coefficients between the two action formulas.

speaker: A. A. Migdal
title: Why quarks suggest local colour gauge fields
summary: Migdal's short discussion begins after Novikov's variations on P000669. It moves from three-quark nucleons and quark--antiquark mesons to short-distance freedom, confinement, relativistic locality and the colour/flavour matrix. No QCD field equation is actually written. Its force-law and uncertainty-principle slogans are not mathematical confinement proofs. The matrix uses three light flavours and three colours; it should not be interpreted as nine independent flavours or as an exhaustive 1976 particle inventory. Bernstein's dated 18/X-76 lecture starts only on P000670 and is outside this record.
